subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Tension: Pulling Apart
description: A fast breakdown of Tension: Pulling Apart for builders.

hook.text: A crane cable holds a ten-ton steel beam in the air. Every fiber in that cable is being pulled apart by tension.

buildup.text: Tensile stress pulls atoms apart. The material elongates in the direction of the force and gets slightly thinner sideways.

discovery.text: The ratio of sideways thinning to lengthwise stretching is Poisson's ratio. Most metals have a value near 0.3.

twist.text: Auxetic materials have a negative Poisson's ratio. Pull them and they get thicker sideways. They defy normal expectations.

climax.text: Tension governs cables, bolts, and chains. If the tensile stress exceeds the material's limit, the part fractures.

punchline.text: Pull it. It stretches, thins, and eventually breaks. Know the limit.

quiz.question: What is Poisson's ratio?
options: The maximum stress a material can handle before fracture
The ratio of sideways thinning to lengthwise stretching under tension
The speed at which a crack travels through a material
